correctness.rationale: For a linear host (0...q-1)^k, the greedy earliest-occurrence argument uses 1 plus linear weak descents blocks; over rotations a nonconstant circular word has an ascent so the worst rotation uses 1+c(u) blocks, whereas a constant word of length h needs h copies. The trace tr(M_q(z)^h) marks cyclic weak descents; Burnside counts a d-fold repetition by substituting z^d and weights phi(d)/h, with the q correction at h=k. Strictly increasing runs between cyclic weak descents have length<=q, proving h<=q(k-1) and the (2,2) boundary exception. For q>=3 and deficit<=2<q, no false new boundary ascent can occur, so one/two missing-symbol cyclic arc configurations yield the three top-layer formulas. Independently enumerated every query necklace and each rotation against the fixed host for (q,k)=(2,2),(2,3),(3,3), confirming the exact weak-descent criterion, support and top length. All-parameter proof is the structural argument, not finite tests.
